Journey's End
A wet rope slides across calloused fingers as the Traveler pulls in the day's catch. Salty water streams off the hooked fish while it tugs 
upwards, rising up the sheer granite cliff to the Traveler's simple wooden hut. Its blue scales glinting in the high noon sun, a small crab 
desperately clinging onto the fish's red finned tail.  "Well then, looks like we have a little traveler of our own." Plucking the crab from 
their catch to throw it off the cliff into the crashing waves below, the Traveler felt fairly confident that its hard shell will allow the critter to 
survive the fall. Letting out a relaxed sigh, they then pull out a thin descaling knife from their Maker's Kit and prepares the fish for lunch. 
 
Humming a song from a distant land, the quiet peace is broken by an erupting cacophony of gulls. Clutching the knife in alarm the Traveler quickly 
stands up and steps over to the cliff to view the distant rocky outcroppings below, expecting the worst this island can offer. Dozens of black beaked fingulls 
shriek and fly haphazardly away from the splashing commotion as black webbed wings beat furiously at the water surface, thrashing violently. 
Yelling in alarm the Traveler runs back to their hut. Quickly rummaging near the door they grip the bone and coral bow, pulling the gut string from their 
belt pouch, rushing to help.  Within moments the Traveler stands alert at the cliff edge, an arrow knocked and trained on the winged beast, waiting for 
the right time to let loose. With a triumphant cry, the skyelarx pulls itself out of the water, its wide wings beating powerfully, struggling to lift itself and 
the dead weight of its prey. Lowering their arrow and smirking, the Traveler watches their winged friend awkwardly fly back home with a long daellash 
hanging limp in its clawed talons.
 
With a wet crash the massive eel drops onto the flagstones near the fire and the skyelarx nimbly lands next to it, its golden eyes clearly pleased with itself 
as it compares the Traveler's meager half-descaled catch to its own.  "Alright, alright, you win. Let me get my knife and we can both eat well tonight."
